title: The symmetric monoidal structure on $\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a symmetric monoidal category with coequalizers such that $X\otimes-$
and $-\otimes X$ preserve colimits for every $X$, and let $\mathcal R$ be a commutative
monoid object. The braiding $\beta_{M,N}\colon M\otimes N\to N\otimes M$ of $\mathcal C$
descends to an isomorphism of $\mathcal R$-module objects
$$
M\otimes_{\mathcal R}N\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }N\otimes_{\mathcal R}M
$$
for the relative tensor product of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. These isomorphisms
make $(\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C),\otimes_{\mathcal R},\mathcal R)$ a symmetric
monoidal category.

proof.text: Write $q_{M,N}:M\otimes N\to M\otimes_{\mathcal R}N$ for the coequalizer projection in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] and $\rho_M=\gamma_M\beta_{M,\mathcal R}$. A coequalizer projection $q$ is epi: if $u q=v q$, uniqueness in its universal property gives $u=v$. Each tensoring functor preserves this coequalizer, so $X\otimes q$ and $q\otimes X$ are also coequalizer projections and hence epi by the same argument. Composites of these projections are epi, since cancellation can be applied successively. Below juxtaposition of maps denotes composition, with the rightmost map applied first; associators in the displayed abbreviated composites are inserted as in the defining parallel pair. The calculations use naturality and the two hexagon axioms, not a replacement of the category by a strict one.

source.place: second paragraph (expanded universal-property and coherence calculations)

proof.text: For the descent calculation, put $a=\rho_M\otimes N$ and $b=M\otimes\gamma_N$, with their defining associator, and let $t=\beta_{\mathcal R\otimes M,N}(\beta_{M,\mathcal R}\otimes N)$, a map from $M\otimes\mathcal R\otimes N$ to $N\otimes\mathcal R\otimes M$. Naturality gives $\beta_{M,N}a=(N\otimes\gamma_M)t$ and $\beta_{M,N}b=(\gamma_N\otimes M)\beta_{M,\mathcal R\otimes N}$. Expanding the two block braidings by their hexagon axioms and cancelling $\beta_{N,\mathcal R}\beta_{\mathcal R,N}=1$ gives $(\beta_{N,\mathcal R}\otimes M)t=\beta_{M,\mathcal R\otimes N}$. The defining relation of $q_{N,M}$ in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] is $q_{N,M}(N\otimes\gamma_M)=q_{N,M}(\gamma_N\otimes M)(\beta_{N,\mathcal R}\otimes M)$. Thus $q_{N,M}\beta_{M,N}a=q_{N,M}\beta_{M,N}b$. The coequalizer universal property defines a unique map $c_{M,N}$ satisfying $c_{M,N}q_{M,N}=q_{N,M}\beta_{M,N}$.

The action $\lambda_{M,N}$ on the relative tensor product in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] satisfies $\lambda_{M,N}(\mathcal R\otimes q_{M,N})=q_{M,N}(\gamma_M\otimes N)$. Precompose the proposed module-linearity equation $c_{M,N}\lambda_{M,N}=\lambda_{N,M}(\mathcal R\otimes c_{M,N})$ with $\mathcal R\otimes q_{M,N}$, an epi by step 1. Its left side becomes
$$q_{N,M}\beta_{M,N}(\gamma_M\otimes N)=q_{N,M}(N\otimes\gamma_M)\beta_{\mathcal R\otimes M,N}=q_{N,M}(\gamma_N\otimes M)(\beta_{N,\mathcal R}\otimes M)\beta_{\mathcal R\otimes M,N}=q_{N,M}(\gamma_N\otimes M)(\mathcal R\otimes\beta_{M,N}).$$
The first equality is naturality, the second is the coequalizer relation, and the third follows by the hexagon expansion $\beta_{\mathcal R\otimes M,N}=(\beta_{\mathcal R,N}\otimes M)(\mathcal R\otimes\beta_{M,N})$ and symmetry. The last expression is the right side after that same precomposition. Cancel the epi. Consequently $c_{M,N}$ is an $\mathcal R$-module morphism.

source.place: second paragraph (expanded universal-property and coherence calculations)

proof.text: For module maps $f:M\to M'$ and $g:N\to N'$, precomposing naturality of $c$ with $q_{M,N}$ reduces it to $q_{N',M'}(g\otimes f)\beta_{M,N}=q_{N',M'}\beta_{M',N'}(f\otimes g)$, which is ambient naturality. Here the induced relative-tensor map is characterized by its composite with $q$ by the defining coequalizer in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Also $c_{N,M}c_{M,N}q_{M,N}=q_{M,N}\beta_{N,M}\beta_{M,N}=q_{M,N}$. Cancel $q_{M,N}$. Interchanging $M,N$ yields $c_{M,N}c_{N,M}=1$ as well. Thus these are natural isomorphisms with inverse $c_{N,M}$.

source.place: second paragraph (expanded universal-property and coherence calculations)

proof.text: Use the associator induced from the ambient associator in [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. For the hexagon that moves $M$ past $N\otimes P$, precompose both sides with the epi $q_{M\otimes_{\mathcal R}N,P}(q_{M,N}\otimes P)$, with ambient reassociation as necessary. Set $Q=q_{N,P\otimes_{\mathcal R}M}(N\otimes q_{P,M})$. By the defining equations of $c$ and of that associator the two composites are $Q\beta_{M,N\otimes P}$ and $Q(N\otimes\beta_{M,P})(\beta_{M,N}\otimes P)$, equal by the first ambient hexagon. For the other hexagon, which moves $M\otimes N$ past $P$, use the same epi and $Q'=q_{P\otimes_{\mathcal R}M,N}(q_{P,M}\otimes N)$. The two composites are $Q'\beta_{M\otimes N,P}$ and $Q'(\beta_{M,P}\otimes N)(M\otimes\beta_{N,P})$, equal by the second ambient hexagon. Cancel the epis in both cases. The relative unitors $l_M,r_M$, induced from the regular bimodule, satisfy $l_Mq_{\mathcal R,M}=\gamma_M$ and $r_Mq_{M,\mathcal R}=\rho_M$. Hence $l_Mc_{M,\mathcal R}q_{M,\mathcal R}=\gamma_M\beta_{M,\mathcal R}=\rho_M=r_Mq_{M,\mathcal R}$, giving the unit compatibility by cancellation. Together with step 4 this supplies the symmetric monoidal structure asserted in the item.
